canonical_homes.name: uniqueSorted
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: Set-dedupe plus sort.Strings, skipping empty strings, always returning a non-nil slice. This is the repairvalidation body verbatim (already_green.go:442), observationally identical to the knowledgecommands body (interview_commands.go:1337). Parameter is `values []string`, not `paths`, because repairvalidation/already_green.go:283 calls it on reason codes, not paths.
canonical_homes.why: Duplicators are corehelpers, knowledgecommands and repairvalidation (finalization is excluded, see D4). Verified with go list -deps at HEAD: knowledgecommands does NOT import corehelpers (its whole closure is resultmodel, commandruntime, ownedprocess, gittransaction, settingshooks) and repairvalidation does NOT import corehelpers either. The request's corehelpers home therefore fails the request's own criterion for two of three duplicators, and would add 9 transitive packages to knowledgecommands and 4 to repairvalidation. resultmodel is in the closure of all three, its own closure is only itself, and all five calling files already import it, so this home costs zero new package edges and zero new import lines.

canonical_homes.name: subtractPaths
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: Set-difference preserving left's order and left's duplicates, returning a non-nil empty slice when nothing survives. Use the finalization body (finalization_prepare.go:365), which builds the membership set inline. The corehelpers body is behaviourally identical but calls the package-local stringSet helper, which resultmodel does not have.
canonical_homes.why: Only two copies and they are behaviourally identical, so this is a pure lift with no semantic decision. corehelpers would also work (finalization already imports it), but finalization_prepare.go imports neither corehelpers nor resultmodel today, so both homes cost exactly one new import line in that file. Keeping SubtractPaths next to UniqueSorted avoids splitting the two path helpers that are called together at finalization_prepare.go:162. corehelpers keeps stringSet, still used at checks.go:319 and inventory.go:425.

canonical_homes.name: firstError
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: Return the first argument when it is non-nil, otherwise the second. Both existing bodies are byte-identical including parameter names, so there is nothing to reconcile.
canonical_homes.why: publication does NOT import corehelpers at HEAD (verified with go list -deps); adding that edge would pull 6 new transitive packages into publication for a five-line function. resultmodel is already in publication's closure. All four call sites use the result only to build the evidence string of a resultmodel finding or refusal, so resultmodel is also where the value is consumed. Costs three new per-file import lines (capture_files.go, answer.go, release.go) and zero new package edges.

canonical_homes.name: compareSemver
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: The knowledgecommands body verbatim (interview_commands.go:1535): split on ".", compare up to three components with strconv.Atoi errors ignored (a non-integer component counts as zero), negative when the FIRST argument is older. Standard Go three-way-compare orientation.
canonical_homes.why: The request names no home for compareSemver at all. knowledgecommands and publication do not import each other, and neither imports corehelpers, so corehelpers is not available. Their shared closure is resultmodel, commandruntime, ownedprocess and gittransaction; resultmodel is the lowest (closure is itself) and both calling files can reach it. The standard orientation is chosen because it is what the name means everywhere else in Go; publication's inverted orientation is preserved at its one call site by rewriting the predicate, not by inverting the helper (decision D2).

canonical_homes.name: requestIDLess
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: The existing repositorymodel body exported in place, unchanged: parse both sides with requestNumberFromText (regexp `(?i)^REQ-0*([0-9]+)`, anchored only at the start); if both parse and the numbers differ, order numerically; otherwise fall back to raw string comparison. requestNumberFromText stays private.
canonical_homes.why: The request is right here. Verified at HEAD: dependency_graph.go:10 and next_types.go:10 both import repositorymodel directly, and the two files holding the call sites (dependency_graph.go, next_targets.go) already import it, so this home costs zero new import lines and zero new package edges. repositorymodel is the leaf of the three (closure is atomicfile, requestmodel, schemanormalization) so no cycle is possible.

canonical_homes.name: physicalPath
canonical_homes.exported_name: physicalPath (stays private in knowledgecommands; suiteinstall's copy is renamed existingPhysicalPath)
canonical_homes.home_package: knowledgecommands (no shared home; the two contracts stay in their own packages under two names)
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: knowledgecommands keeps `physicalPath`: walk upward with os.Lstat collecting missing components, EvalSymlinks the deepest existing ancestor, re-join and Clean. Absence is normal, result is not forced absolute. suiteinstall's copy is renamed `existingPhysicalPath` with its body unchanged: filepath.EvalSymlinks then filepath.Abs, absence is an error, result is always absolute.
canonical_homes.why: The one name where a single canonical definition cannot preserve both callers. suiteinstall/update_transaction.go:179 uses the missing-path ERROR as its existence check for the installed skill, and needs filepath.Abs because line 183 feeds the result into strings.HasPrefix(skillRoot, projectRoot+separator) with a user-supplied --skill-root that may be relative. knowledgecommands/commands.go:144 (ensureSafeTarget, feeding bkb-init, bkb-scan, dream-scan) needs absence to SUCCEED because the target is about to be created; any error becomes the BKB-INIT-UNSAFE-TARGET refusal. Merging needs a mode flag plus a new import edge for two packages that share only resultmodel, commandruntime and settingshooks, none a plausible home for a filesystem helper. Renaming suiteinstall's copy is 4 line touches, zero behaviour change, zero new imports, and leaves the one test that names the helper (memory_commands_test.go:390) untouched.

reconciliations.name: D1 — empty-string handling in uniqueSorted
reconciliations.decision: The canonical resultmodel.UniqueSorted DROPS empty strings.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: knowledgecommands (6 calls in interview_commands.go, 2 in memory_commands.go) and repairvalidation (5 calls in already_green.go) keep byte-identical behaviour — their current bodies already drop empties and are observationally identical to each other. corehelpers (4 calls in checks.go at 741, 782, 804, 906; 2 in inventory.go at 419, 460) keeps identical behaviour on every reachable input: I read all six producers at HEAD and each filters empties before the call — backtickedPathsOnLine skips empty segments (checks.go:751), firstBacktickedPaths guards with `if rest[:second] != ""` (checks.go:779), allBacktickedPaths guards with `if parts[index] != ""` (checks.go:799), porcelainPaths errors on records shorter than 4 bytes and on a missing rename origin (checks.go:894-903), inventory.go:419 unions nonblankLines output with readInventory rows whose Path is record[3:] of a len>=4 record, and newlineList (inventory.go:460) is called only with those two already-filtered lists. Drop-empty preserves 13 of the 19 call sites byte-exactly against 6 for keep-empty, and an empty string is not a valid path or reason code at any of the 19.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: If a producer ever starts emitting an empty string, the corehelpers scope-drift and protected-inventory paths would silently lose it instead of reporting it. Nothing in the tree can produce one today, and no test pins either behaviour, so the suite will not catch a mistake here.

reconciliations.name: D2 — unparseable semver, and the inverted sign the request does not mention
reconciliations.decision: The canonical resultmodel.CompareSemver is LENIENT (Atoi errors count as zero, a shorter string is compared only across the components both sides have) and uses the STANDARD orientation (negative when the first argument is older). publication keeps its strictness at the call site, not in the helper: its existing parseSemver stays in publication/release.go and is hoisted into the predicate.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: knowledgecommands/interview_commands.go:820 keeps byte-identical behaviour: same body, same `< 0` predicate, only the package qualifier is added. publication/release.go:26 keeps byte-identical behaviour with `if compareSemver(oldVersion, newVersion) != 1 {` rewritten to `_, oldParsed := parseSemver(oldVersion); _, newParsed := parseSemver(newVersion); if !oldParsed || !newParsed || resultmodel.CompareSemver(oldVersion, newVersion) >= 0 {` guarding the same RELEASE-VERSION-NOT-INCREASING refusal. I compiled both predicates and compared them over 361 table pairs (including "1.0", "9", "abc", "", "01.2.3", "1.a.0", "1.0.0.0", negative components) plus 200,000 random three-component version pairs: zero differences.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: The two copies return OPPOSITE signs for every unequal pair — the request describes this as a parse-strictness difference and never mentions the inversion. If the merge is done by picking one body and leaving both predicates alone, publication/release.go:26 starts ACCEPTING version downgrades (2.0.0 -> 1.0.0) and REFUSING every legitimate increase, and knowledgecommands/interview_commands.go:820 starts writing an older template version into the session. No test in internal/ exercises compareSemver, parseSemver or semverMajor, so both bugs would ship green.

reconciliations.name: D3 — requestIDLess number parsing
reconciliations.decision: The canonical repositorymodel.RequestIDLess uses the PERMISSIVE parser (regexp `(?i)^REQ-0*([0-9]+)`, anchored only at the start, so a non-digit tail after the leading digit run is ignored). nextselection's strict whole-remainder parser is not adopted.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: repositorymodel (repository_model.go:305, 319) keeps byte-identical behaviour — same body, only the name changes. dependencygraph (dependency_graph.go:115, 117, 249, 303) keeps byte-identical behaviour: I ran the hand-rolled byte-scan parser (dependency_graph.go:316) against the regexp parser over 8,016 inputs and got 0 disagreements, and compared the two orderings over 160,000 ordered pairs and got 0 disagreements, so deleting dependencygraph's copy plus its requestNumber helper is a provable no-op. nextselection (next_targets.go:97, 151) CHANGES for identifiers shaped REQ-<digits><non-digit tail>: "REQ-2" vs "REQ-12a" currently sorts REQ-12a first (strict parse fails, lexical fallback) and will sort REQ-2 first, which is what repositorymodel and dependencygraph already produce for the same snapshot. nextselection keeps numericID (next_types.go:60) unchanged — it has 9 other uses including the "UR-" prefix at next_targets.go:65.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: This is the only real behaviour change in the plan. It changes the order the `next` queue is considered in for malformed IDs. No such ID exists in the repository's front matter today and no test pins either direction, so a green suite is not evidence the choice was right. The alternative that preserves nextselection exactly is a strictness parameter on RequestIDLess; I rejected it because it is a boolean that exists only to preserve a divergence nothing exercises, and the divergence is itself a bug (two packages ordering one snapshot differently).

reconciliations.name: D4 — finalization's uniqueSorted is not a duplicate, so it is renamed rather than merged
reconciliations.decision: finalization/finalization_prepare.go:379 is renamed to `normalizedUniquePaths` and stays in finalization. It is NOT replaced by resultmodel.UniqueSorted.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: All 22 production call sites (18 in finalization_discovery.go, 1 at finalization_prepare.go:162, 3 in finalization_apply.go) and the one test reference (finalization_recovery_test.go:574) keep byte-identical behaviour — only the identifier changes. The body is `result, _ := normalizeRepositoryPaths(paths); return result`: it is a validator, not a deduper. It rejects empty and absolute paths and paths that escape the repository, returns nil for the WHOLE slice on any single rejection, and rewrites survivors with filepath.Clean and filepath.ToSlash. Folding it into the canonical would change every one of those 22 sites, and five of them turn the nil into a silently skipped safety check rather than a refusal — most visibly finalization_prepare.go:162, where the "commit_paths omits planned lifecycle or release targets" guard would flip from silently passing to keeping the paths.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: A reviewer reading "delete the other eight definitions" literally may reject a rename. The counter-argument is that the request's own Why calls this class "same name, different contract" — the collision is the name, and renaming resolves it at zero behavioural cost, while merging costs the same number of line touches AND changes 22 call sites. Separately, the discarded error at line 379 is a genuine defect (line 153 of the same function calls normalizeRepositoryPaths directly and DOES propagate the same error); that is out of scope here and should be captured as a discovered task.

reconciliations.name: D5 — missing-ancestor paths: physicalPath stays two functions
reconciliations.decision: No merge. suiteinstall/update_transaction.go:209 is renamed `existingPhysicalPath`; knowledgecommands/commands.go:147 keeps the name `physicalPath`. Neither is exported and no import edge is added.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: suiteinstall (update_transaction.go:175, 179, 199) keeps byte-identical behaviour: absence is an error, result is always absolute via filepath.Abs. knowledgecommands (commands.go:144, memory_commands.go:1216 and 1227, interview_commands.go:396 and 683) keeps byte-identical behaviour: absence succeeds and synthesizes the path the caller will create, result is Clean but not forced absolute. The only test that names the helper, memory_commands_test.go:390, stays untouched because the copy it calls keeps its name.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: The two contracts are irreconcilable on two axes at once, not one. Axis 1: suiteinstall/update_transaction.go:179 uses the missing-path error AS the existence check for the installed skill, while knowledgecommands/commands.go:144 resolves a target about to be created and maps any error to the BKB-INIT-UNSAFE-TARGET refusal — a merged erroring contract would refuse every genuinely new knowledge base and blame a symlink for a merely absent path. Axis 2, which the request does not name: the knowledgecommands body has no filepath.Abs, so a merged walking contract would return a relative path for a relative --skill-root, and the next guard at line 183 would falsely refuse a legitimate update with "skill is outside this project". If the maintainer insists on a single definition, it needs a mode flag and a much larger risk budget.

lock_in_design:
One assertion appended to /home/user/skill-do-work/_dev/tests/audit-lockins.sh, in the same shape as the blocks already there (compute into a variable, compare, printf FAIL to stderr, increment failure_count). It counts non-test Go function definitions across $repo_root/skills whose name is one of the six helper names in either the private or the exported casing, and fails unless the total is exactly 6.

Regex, anchored with no prefix wildcard:
^func (uniqueSorted|UniqueSorted|subtractPaths|SubtractPaths|requestIDLess|RequestIDLess|firstError|FirstError|compareSemver|CompareSemver|physicalPath|PhysicalPath)\(

Measured at HEAD a48b9eb: 15 matches. After steps 1-10: 6 matches, one per name — resultmodel.UniqueSorted, resultmodel.SubtractPaths, resultmodel.FirstError, resultmodel.CompareSemver, repositorymodel.RequestIDLess, knowledgecommands.physicalPath. The two renamed-out functions (finalization.normalizedUniquePaths, suiteinstall.existingPhysicalPath) do not match, which is the point: they are different contracts and must not be counted as copies of these names.

Three design choices worth defending in review. First, the anchor `^func (` with no leading wildcard is mandatory — publication/defer_gate.go:526 already defines appendUniqueSorted, and a loose regex counts it and pins the wrong number (16 instead of 15 today). Second, both casings are listed so that re-introducing a private uniqueSorted next to the exported one goes red immediately rather than after someone notices. Third, the awk sums rg -c output and prints `total + 0`, so a scan that matches nothing yields 0 and still fails; the assertion cannot decay into a silent pass if the tree layout changes. rg exits 1 on no matches, which is harmless because the file uses `set -uo pipefail` without `-e` and the pipeline runs inside a command substitution.

Scope note: the count covers $repo_root/skills, which is wider than the REQ's Reproduce command (do-work-cli/internal only). Both give 15 today — I checked that skills/do-work-board/tools/queue-kanban defines none of the six names (its only hits are local variables named firstError in test files, which the --glob '!*_test.go' filter excludes anyway). The wider scope also catches regrowth in the Kanban Go tool.
risks: R1 (highest, settle before coding). resultmodel is the CLI result and rendering model, and this plan puts four generic helpers in it. That is a fit compromise made to satisfy the request's own no-new-edges criterion, which corehelpers cannot satisfy: knowledgecommands, repairvalidation and publication do not import corehelpers at HEAD. Numbers if the maintainer overrules me and wants corehelpers: knowledgecommands' closure goes from 5 to 14 packages, repairvalidation gains 4, publication gains 6, and 6 new import lines are needed instead of 4. No import cycle either way — corehelpers' closure contains none of those three packages, verified with go list -deps.

R2. Decision D3 changes nextselection's queue ordering for identifiers shaped REQ-<digits><non-digit tail>, and the REQ's constraints forbid the Go test that would pin it ("no test file changes beyond the lock-in"). No such identifier exists in the repository's front matter today and no existing test constrains the choice in either direction, so go test ./... will be green whichever parser survives. A green suite is not evidence this decision was right. This is the largest uncovered risk in the REQ, and the constraints are what leave it uncovered.

R3. The publication/release.go:26 predicate rewrite is the only place a caller's control flow text changes rather than just gaining a package qualifier. I verified equivalence over 361 table pairs plus 200,000 random version triples with zero differences, but it is the one edit a reviewer must read line by line, because getting the sign wrong there silently accepts a version downgrade in release planning.

R4. Two of the six survivors deviate from the request's letter. knowledgecommands.physicalPath stays private and unexported (D5) because it is not shared with anything, and finalization's copy is renamed rather than deleted (D4). The request says "one canonical definition per name, exported" and "delete the other eight". A reviewer reading that literally can reject the plan. The defence is that both renamed functions are different contracts, not copies, and that merging either changes 22 and 3 call sites respectively for no benefit.

R5. Two deletions leave an import unused and break the build if the import is not removed in the same step: "strconv" in dependencygraph/dependency_graph.go after requestNumber goes (line 328 is its only use), and "sort" in repairvalidation/already_green.go after uniqueSorted goes (line 453 is its only use). Both are named in steps 3 and 6. Every other import stays used — I checked each one.

R6. The finalization rename touches 24 lines across four files including a test file. Done with a word-boundary sed scoped to internal/finalization/ it is safe; done by hand a missed site is a compile error, so it fails loudly rather than silently.

R7. The REQ's own numbers will not match after this. The count is 15 at HEAD, not 14 (the extra copy is repairvalidation/already_green.go:442, a package REQ-557 never mentions), so it is nine deletions-or-renames, not eight. The declared 10-file write_set is short by nine files and lists one file this plan does not need (knowledgecommands/commands.go). Expected net line delta will be near break-even rather than the -70 the REQ predicts, because roughly 45 call sites gain a package qualifier and the canonical bodies are added back in resultmodel.

R8. The audited commit dc8a64e3 is not an object in this clone (git cat-file -t dc8a64e3 fails). Every fact in this plan was re-derived at HEAD a48b9eb with a clean working tree, and the two equivalence claims the plan depends on were measured with a compiled differential probe rather than taken from the request or from earlier surveys.

canonical_homes.name: uniqueSorted
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: Pure dedupe + sort. Keeps EVERY value verbatim including the empty string, applies no path cleaning, always returns a non-nil slice (make([]string,0,len(set))). Signature `UniqueSortedStrings(values []string) []string` — parameter is `values`, not `paths`, because repairvalidation/already_green.go:283 passes ReasonCodes (the literals REPAIR-CANONICAL-COMPLETION-REFUSED and REPAIR-STAGED-PATH-NOT-CANONICAL), not paths. Verified by reading that line.
canonical_homes.why: The request routes this to corehelpers. I verified with `go list -deps` at HEAD that corehelpers is NOT in the dependency closure of knowledgecommands (closure: resultmodel commandruntime ownedprocess gittransaction settingshooks) or repairvalidation (closure: resultmodel commandruntime atomicfile schemanormalization requestmodel repositorymodel dependencygraph gateevidence ownedprocess gittransaction requeststate). So corehelpers violates the request's own 'a package the duplicator already imports' rule for two of the four duplicators, and importing it would add 9 transitive packages to knowledgecommands (dependencygraph, requeststate, cleanup, doctor, nextselection among them) that it does not use. The only packages all four duplicators already import are resultmodel, commandruntime, ownedprocess and gittransaction — resultmodel is a pure serialization DTO package, commandruntime is the dispatcher, ownedprocess is process-group control, gittransaction is git plumbing. Putting a string-set helper in any of them is a junk drawer with maximal blast radius. A new zero-internal-dependency leaf adds exactly one import edge per duplicator, cannot participate in a cycle by construction, and is cheaper than every compliant alternative. Semantics: 'keep everything' is the honest primitive. The knowledgecommands and repairvalidation copies drop the empty string silently; that is a lenient contract that would swallow a producer bug without telling anyone. I confirmed the drop is dead code today by reading the producers (repairvalidation/already_green.go:404 guards len(record) >= 4 before record[3:]; :416 passes strings.FieldsFunc output, which never emits empty fields; every knowledgecommands site passes filepath.Join/ToSlash map keys or filepath.Dir output, none of which can be ""), so choosing 'keep' changes nothing observable at any of the 42 call sites while removing the silent swallow.

canonical_homes.name: subtractPaths
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: `SubtractStringValues(leftValues, rightValues []string) []string` — builds a membership map from rightValues inline, returns the elements of leftValues not in it, preserving leftValues' order AND its duplicates, returning a non-nil empty slice when nothing survives. The set is built inline, not via corehelpers' stringSet.
canonical_homes.why: corehelpers WOULD be a compliant home for this one name (finalization already imports corehelpers and calls corehelpers.ReadProtectedInventory at finalization_apply.go:467). I put it in the leaf anyway so it stays beside UniqueSortedStrings — the two are called together at finalization_prepare.go:162 and read as one pair. Behaviour: I diffed the two bodies (corehelpers/checks.go:827-836 vs finalization/finalization_prepare.go:365-376); they are algorithmically identical, differing only in that corehelpers calls the local stringSet helper and finalization inlines the map. The canonical version must inline it: corehelpers/checks.go:855 stringSet has two other callers (checks.go:319, inventory.go:425) so it stays where it is and must NOT be moved.

canonical_homes.name: firstError
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: `FirstNonNilError(firstCandidate, secondCandidate error) error` — returns firstCandidate when it is non-nil, otherwise secondCandidate. Unchanged from both existing copies.
canonical_homes.why: I printed both bodies (corehelpers/checks.go:871 and publication/capture_files.go:361): byte-identical, same parameter names. Zero behaviour risk, pure lift. The request routes it to corehelpers, but publication does not import corehelpers (verified closure: atomicfile resultmodel commandruntime ownedprocess gittransaction releaseownership schemanormalization requestmodel repositorymodel), so corehelpers is again non-compliant with the request's own rule and would add 6 transitive packages to publication. Naming: `firstError` fails Naming for Reach (one word plus a bare noun, and 'first error' reads as 'the error that happened first' rather than 'the first candidate that is not nil'). FirstNonNilError says what it does and is greppable.

canonical_homes.name: compareSemver
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: `CompareSemanticVersions(leftVersion, rightVersion string) (ordering int, parsed bool)`. STANDARD Go orientation: negative when leftVersion is older. STRICT parse (publication's parseSemver rules, lifted verbatim): exactly three dot-separated parts, no empty part, no leading zero on a multi-character part, integer only, non-negative. When either side fails to parse, parsed is false and ordering is 0 — the caller must decide, and cannot mistake 'unparseable' for 'equal'. Also exports `ParseSemanticVersion(version string) ([3]int, bool)` so publication's release_mirrors.go:109 validator keeps working after publication's private parseSemver is deleted.
canonical_homes.why: There is NO package that both duplicators already import and that could sanely hold a version comparator — knowledgecommands and publication share only resultmodel, commandruntime, ownedprocess and gittransaction, and the request assigns no canonical home for this name at all. The leaf is the only honest answer. On semantics: the two copies are INVERTED, which the request never mentions. I read both bodies. knowledgecommands/interview_commands.go:1535 returns -1 when a[index] < b[index], i.e. -1 when the FIRST argument is older (standard). publication/release.go:210 returns +1 when newParts[index] > oldParts[index], i.e. +1 when the SECOND argument is newer. For (1.0.0, 1.1.0) they return opposite signs. Any de-duplication that picks one body by name alone corrupts one caller silently. I chose the standard Go orientation because it matches cmp.Compare and because publication's caller predicate can be rewritten to an exactly equivalent set (proof under reconciliations). I chose the strict parse because knowledgecommands' `ai, _ := strconv.Atoi(a[index])` discards a real parse error and fabricates an ordering: today compareSemver("1.a.0", "1.2.0") returns -1 and the session stamp is bumped on the strength of a number that was never there. The explicit `parsed` return is the fix: it forces both callers to say what they do with garbage instead of guessing.

canonical_homes.name: physicalPath
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: `ResolvePhysicalPath(candidatePath string) (string, error)` — the knowledgecommands walking contract PLUS the filepath.Abs the knowledgecommands copy is missing. Walk upward with os.Lstat collecting basenames of components that do not exist; stop at the first existing ancestor (error on a non-ENOENT stat error, or when filepath.Dir stops changing); filepath.EvalSymlinks that ancestor; re-join the collected components in reverse; filepath.Clean; then filepath.Abs. Absence is NOT an error. The result is ALWAYS absolute.
canonical_homes.why: knowledgecommands and suiteinstall share only resultmodel, commandruntime and settingshooks; corehelpers is in neither closure. Leaf again. On semantics the request names one contract axis; there are two. Axis 1 (named): suiteinstall/update_transaction.go:209 is EvalSymlinks+Abs and errors on absence; knowledgecommands/commands.go:147 walks missing ancestors and succeeds. Axis 2 (NOT named, and live): the knowledgecommands copy ends at filepath.Clean with no filepath.Abs, so it returns a RELATIVE path for a relative existing input. I traced --skill-root: suiteinstall/suite_commands.go:163-166 takes it straight from the user flag and only falls back to an absolute default when empty, and update_transaction.go:183 feeds the result into `strings.HasPrefix(skillRoot, projectRoot+string(filepath.Separator))` against an absolute projectRoot. A relative result there produces the false refusal 'skill is outside this project'. So the merged helper must keep Abs. I chose the walking contract as canonical because absence-is-an-error is a caller's assertion, not a resolver's job, and today suiteinstall smuggles its existence check into EvalSymlinks' ENOENT — the error it raises ('the installed do-work skill could not be located') is literally an existence claim wearing a resolver's clothes. The walking contract is also mandatory for knowledgecommands/commands.go:144 (ensureSafeTarget resolves a target that is about to be CREATED; under the strict contract every `bkb-init` on a new knowledge base would refuse with BKB-INIT-UNSAFE-TARGET and blame a symlink for a path that is merely absent). Adding Abs is free for knowledgecommands: I read all five of its call sites and every one already passes an absolute path (commands.go:144 joins onto filepath.Abs(root); interview_commands.go:396 and memory_commands.go:1216 pass RepositoryRoot; memory_commands.go:1227 and interview_commands.go:683 Join onto an absolute base when the input is relative).

canonical_homes.name: requestIDLess
canonical_homes.home_package: internal/repositorymodel (EXISTING — the request's proposal, confirmed correct)
canonical_homes.chosen_semantics: Keep repositorymodel's body verbatim, exported: parse both sides with requestNumberFromText (regexp `(?i)^REQ-0*([0-9]+)`, anchored at the start only, so a trailing non-digit tail is ignored — 'REQ-12a' parses as 12); if both parse and the numbers differ, compare numerically; otherwise fall back to raw string comparison. The PERMISSIVE parser wins.
canonical_homes.why: This is the one home the request gets right and it is right for a structural reason, not a majority vote. I verified with `go list -deps` and by reading the import blocks: dependencygraph imports repositorymodel (dependency_graph.go:10), nextselection imports repositorymodel (next_types.go:10), and repositorymodel's whole internal closure is atomicfile, requestmodel, schemanormalization — it is already the leaf, so no cycle is possible. On semantics: repositorymodel's requestNumberFromText is the parser that ASSIGNS identity elsewhere in the same file — requestIDFromText -> formatRequestID("REQ-%03d") produces FilenameID at repository_model.go:526 and the collision keys at :284. A comparator that disagrees with the identity parser can order the raw id and its canonical form differently for the same request. dependencygraph's hand-rolled byte scan (dependency_graph.go:316) is exactly equivalent to it (I read both: same start-anchoring, same case-insensitivity, same 'at least one digit' rule, and the regex's `0*` strips zeros that Atoi would have absorbed anyway), so folding dependencygraph in is a no-op. nextselection's numericID (next_types.go:60) is the odd one out: it rejects the identifier if ANY character after the prefix is a non-digit. It stays in nextselection — it has seven other callers (next_targets.go:29, 41, 47, 65, 72, 104, 127, 167 and canonicalToken at next_types.go:76, including the 'UR-' prefix) where strict validation of a CLI target token is the correct job. Only its use as a sort comparator goes away.

reconciliations.name: D1 — uniqueSorted: the empty string is kept, never silently dropped
reconciliations.decision: The canonical UniqueSortedStrings preserves every value it is given, including "". It dedupes and sorts and does nothing else. The empty-string filters in knowledgecommands/interview_commands.go:1337 and repairvalidation/already_green.go:442 are deleted, not preserved.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: Every one of the 42 call sites keeps its exact current output. corehelpers (6 sites) already had keep-everything semantics — unchanged by construction. knowledgecommands (8 sites) and repairvalidation (5 sites) lose a filter that cannot fire: I read each producer at HEAD — repairvalidation/already_green.go:404 appends record[3:] only when len(record) >= 4, :416 passes strings.FieldsFunc output which by definition contains no empty field, :266 draws from dryRun.Changes[].Path whose only nullable fields are guarded by explicit != "" checks in requeststate/state_plan.go:451 and :455, :283 passes two string literals; every knowledgecommands site passes mapKeysBytes over maps whose keys are filepath.Join/filepath.ToSlash results or filepath.Dir output, none of which can return "". The nil-vs-empty contract is also preserved: all three surviving semantics return non-nil, which matters at repairvalidation/already_green.go:283-284 where the result is assigned into validation.ReasonCodes and validation.OffendingPaths and serialized — a nil would render as JSON null instead of [].
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: If a producer I traced can in fact emit "", a blank entry now appears in an evidence list or a JSON array instead of vanishing. That is the safe direction — the blank becomes visible to a human or to a downstream guard instead of being swallowed — but it would be a visible output change. The unsafe direction would have been adopting the drop-empty semantics into corehelpers, where scopeDeclaredPaths and allBacktickedPaths carry human-authored REQ markdown and a swallowed entry means SCOPE-UNDECLARED-TOUCH reports nothing.

reconciliations.name: D2 — uniqueSorted: finalization's copy is a validator with its error thrown away; the wrapper is deleted and the one call site that needs the validation gets the error back
reconciliations.decision: finalization/finalization_prepare.go:379 (`result, _ := normalizeRepositoryPaths(paths); return result`) is deleted outright. Its 23 non-test call sites split two ways. finalization_prepare.go:162 — the only site whose result feeds a guard decision — calls normalizeRepositoryPaths DIRECTLY and propagates its error, exactly the way finalization_prepare.go:153 already does nine lines above it in the same function. The other 22 sites call sharedprimitives.UniqueSortedStrings. normalizeRepositoryPaths itself is NOT moved, renamed or changed — it stays private to finalization.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: finalization_prepare.go:162: today, a required commit path that is empty, absolute, ".", ".." or "../…" makes uniqueSorted return nil for the WHOLE slice, so subtractPaths(nil, …) returns empty, len(missing) is 0, and the 'commit_paths omits planned lifecycle or release targets' error at line 164 never fires. After the change the same input returns the normalizeRepositoryPaths error ('path must be non-empty and repository-relative: %s' or 'path escapes repository: %s') up through prepareFinalization, which already returns an error at line 154. Both sides of the comparison stay normalized (effectiveCommitPaths at line 153 and requiredCommitPaths now both go through normalizeRepositoryPaths), so there is no risk of a false 'missing' from an unclean-but-valid path. For every well-formed input the result is byte-identical to today. The other 22 sites are evidence lists (discovery.go:67, 70, 132, 162, 188, 205, 627), deterministic iteration order (discovery.go:844, 1470), journal path lists (discovery.go:194, 195, 1432), return values whose length the caller tests (discovery.go:640, 649, 573, 1422, 895; apply.go:518, 522), and the git-reset argument list (apply.go:233). They lose filepath.Clean + filepath.ToSlash, which is only observable on an unclean input; every one of them is fed git porcelain paths, filepath.Join results, or (at discovery.go:1518) a list the loop at lines 1511-1516 has ALREADY cleaned and validated. In exchange all five nil-producing shapes disappear — apply.go:233 can no longer skip the `git reset -q HEAD --` that clears finalizer-owned index entries during rollback, apply.go:518/522 can no longer skip FINALIZATION-PROTECTED-DECLARED-PATH or FINALIZATION-AMBIGUOUS-SHARED-STATE, and discovery.go:194 can no longer drop a candidate REQ out of `admitted` at line 196 instead of refusing.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: If any journal or manifest path reaching the 22 pure-dedupe sites is genuinely unclean ("do-work/./x", a trailing slash), the evidence string in a refusal changes text and the git-reset argument carries the raw form. Git accepts both. The comparison at finalization_apply.go:514 (`allowed[row.Path]`) is between journal paths and git porcelain rows; git emits forward slashes on every platform and normalizeRepositoryPaths' Clean+ToSlash round-trip was a no-op on already-slashed input, so the set membership is unchanged. The larger residual risk is what this REQ deliberately does not fix: normalizeRepositoryPaths' error is now honoured at prepare.go:162 but the discard pattern is gone rather than generalised — no other site was rewired to propagate errors, because that would change ~20 function signatures and is out of scope.

reconciliations.name: D3 — compareSemver: one orientation (standard Go), one strict parser, and an explicit parsed flag so no caller can read 'unparseable' as 'equal'
reconciliations.decision: CompareSemanticVersions(leftVersion, rightVersion) returns (ordering int, parsed bool) with negative ordering meaning leftVersion is older, and uses publication's strict parseSemver rules verbatim. Both callers are rewritten. publication/release.go:26 becomes `ordering, parsed := sharedprimitives.CompareSemanticVersions(oldVersion, newVersion); if !parsed || ordering >= 0 { refuse RELEASE-VERSION-NOT-INCREASING }`. knowledgecommands/interview_commands.go:820 becomes `ordering, parsed := sharedprimitives.CompareSemanticVersions(old, template.Version); if !parsed { return false, errors.New("template and session versions must be bare semver") }; if ordering < 0 { session["template_version"] = template.Version }` — reusing the error string that already exists at line 814 for the semverMajor failure. knowledgecommands' semverMajor stays (it drives the major-gap migration loop at lines 816-826).
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: publication keeps its behaviour EXACTLY, on every input. Today it refuses unless compareSemver returns +1, and +1 is returned only when both versions parse strictly and new is greater than old on the first differing component. The new predicate refuses unless parsed && ordering < 0, which is the same set: parsed && old < new. A version downgrade is still refused, unparseable input is still refused, equal versions are still refused. knowledgecommands keeps its behaviour on every well-formed input: for two strictly-parseable versions ordering < 0 is true exactly when the session version is older, which is exactly when compareSemver returned -1 today. The ONLY change is the malformed branch. Today `1.a.0` vs `1.2.0` returns -1 through a discarded strconv.Atoi error and the session stamp is bumped on a fabricated ordering; after the change it returns the existing 'template and session versions must be bare semver' error. semverMajor at lines 811-815 already rejects anything that is not three dot-separated parts with an integer first part, so the newly-erroring set is narrow: a leading zero on any component ('01.2.3', '1.02.0'), a non-integer minor or patch ('1.a.0'), a negative component, or an empty component ('1..0'). Every member of that set is genuinely malformed. The shipped template version is 2.0.0 (skills/do-work-knowledge/interviews/work-operating-model.md) and the default when the session carries no stamp is the literal '1.0.0', so no shipped value is affected.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: If a real session on disk carries a version like '01.0.0', interview migration now returns an error where it previously bumped silently. That surfaces as a refusal the user can see and fix, not as data loss — the session file is not written on the error path. The catastrophic risk is the one this decision exists to prevent: picking either body by name alone. Adopting publication's orientation into knowledgecommands makes it write an OLDER template version into the session; adopting knowledgecommands' orientation into publication makes BuildReleasePlan accept a version downgrade (2.0.0 -> 1.0.0) and refuse every legitimate increase. Neither shows up as an error — both are wrong branches — and nothing in internal/ tests compareSemver, parseSemver or semverMajor today (verified: `rg` over all *_test.go returns no hit for any of the three).

reconciliations.name: D4 — physicalPath: one resolver with the permissive walking contract plus Abs; suiteinstall's existence assertions become explicit and keep their exact wording
reconciliations.decision: ResolvePhysicalPath never treats absence as an error and always returns an absolute path. suiteinstall/update_transaction.go regains its existence check as an explicit statement at the one call site whose error IS the check: after `skillRoot, err = sharedprimitives.ResolvePhysicalPath(options.InstalledSkillRoot)`, add `if info, statErr := os.Stat(skillRoot); statErr != nil || !info.IsDir() { return "", "", fmt.Errorf("the installed do-work skill could not be located") }` — the same error string, byte for byte. No check is added at line 175 or line 199.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: suiteinstall keeps all three of its observable behaviours. Line 175 (ProjectRoot): unchanged, because os.Stat + info.IsDir() already guards it three lines earlier at 171-174, so absence never reaches the resolver; the remaining error branch still catches non-ENOENT stat failures. Line 179 (skillRoot): the missing-skill refusal and its exact message are preserved by the new explicit check, and the relative-flag case is FIXED rather than preserved — a relative --skill-root that exists now yields an absolute path and passes the HasPrefix containment guard at line 183 instead of being falsely refused with 'skill is outside this project'. Line 199 (git root): the input is the trimmed output of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` on a directory that has already been stat-verified, so both contracts return the same string; if git ever returned a nonexistent path the equality test at line 203 still refuses, with a different message. knowledgecommands keeps all five of its behaviours unchanged: ensureSafeTarget (commands.go:144) still resolves a target that does not exist yet, so bkb-init, bkb-scan and dream-scan keep working; the symlink confinement it enforces is intact because EvalSymlinks is still applied to the deepest EXISTING ancestor, and you cannot symlink-escape through a component that does not exist; memory_commands.go:1227 still succeeds on a missing memory root so the friendly 'memory root does not exist: %s' at line 1234 keeps firing instead of a raw lstat error; interview_commands.go:683's `if err != nil { continue }` keeps its current near-dead status and the os.Stat + IsDir check keeps doing the filtering. The added filepath.Abs is a no-op at all five, since every input is already absolute.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: The suiteinstall existence check is the whole risk. If it is omitted, a missing --skill-root stops refusing at line 179 and instead refuses later with 'SKILL.md is missing at <synthesized path>' — still a refusal, but blaming the wrong thing, and it would ship unnoticed because nothing pins that string (verified: `rg 'could not be located'` finds no hit in any *_test.go or under _dev/). A new suiteinstall test pinning the message is required, not optional. The second risk is that the walking resolver is more permissive at a site I have not identified as needing strictness — I read all eight non-test call sites and there is no third group, but a future caller inheriting 'absence is fine' from the name is a real hazard, which is why the doc comment must state the contract in one line.

reconciliations.name: D5 — requestIDLess: the permissive parser wins, so a trailing non-digit tail sorts numerically everywhere
reconciliations.decision: One exported repositorymodel.RequestIDLess using requestNumberFromText. nextselection/next_types.go:83 and dependencygraph/dependency_graph.go:307 are deleted, along with dependencygraph's requestNumber (dependency_graph.go:316) which has no other caller. nextselection's numericID is KEPT — it has nine other callers and remains the correct strict validator for CLI target tokens and for the 'UR-' prefix.
reconciliations.behaviour_each_caller_keeps: dependencygraph keeps its behaviour exactly at all four sites (dependency_graph.go:115, 117, 249, 303): its byte-scan parser and repositorymodel's regex return identical (value, ok) pairs — both anchor only at the start, both are case-insensitive, both require at least one digit after 'REQ-', and the regex's `0*` strips zeros Atoi would have absorbed. repositorymodel keeps its behaviour at both sites (:305, :319) since the body is unchanged. nextselection CHANGES at its two sites (next_targets.go:97 and :151). For an id with a non-digit tail, its strict parser used to fail and fall back to byte-wise string comparison; now the tail is ignored and the leading number is compared. Concretely, a queue holding 'REQ-2' and 'REQ-12a' came out of nextselection.Select as [REQ-12a, REQ-2] while repositorymodel's snapshot.RequestFiles and dependencygraph's OrderedIDs both reported [REQ-2, REQ-12a] for the identical snapshot. After the change all three agree. Everything nextselection uses numericID for other than sorting — canonicalToken's 'must be REQ- followed by digits' rejection, target-token validation at next_targets.go:41/47/104/167, UR membership at :65/:72 — is untouched, so a suffixed id is still not a valid CLI target.
reconciliations.risk_if_wrong: This is a correctness fix, not a preference: today one command run can produce two different orderings of the same snapshot, and the tie-break at dependency_graph.go:115 sorts raw `depends_on:` tokens copied straight out of REQ front matter with nothing canonicalising them first. The change is latent in this repository — a front-matter scan of do-work/ found 717 `id:` values and 1,814 dependency tokens with ZERO in the disagreement shape — but reachable, since no Go code validates the `id:` or `depends_on:` shape before these sorts run. The risk of being wrong is that a maintainer WANTS 'REQ-12a' to sort away from 'REQ-12'; the counter-argument is that repositorymodel already collapses 'REQ-12a-foo.md' to FilenameID 'REQ-012' at repository_model.go:526, so a strict comparator disagrees with the identity the same package assigns. Nothing in the suite constrains the choice, so a new test pinning the 'REQ-2' before 'REQ-12a' ordering must ship with it.

ordered_steps.what: Create the leaf package. Four files, no internal imports at all (stdlib only: sort; os and path/filepath; strconv and strings). UniqueSortedStrings and SubtractStringValues in string_value_sets.go; FirstNonNilError in error_selection.go; CompareSemanticVersions and ParseSemanticVersion in semantic_version_order.go; ResolvePhysicalPath in physical_path_resolution.go. Each carries a one-line doc comment stating the contract chosen in D1-D4 — specifically that UniqueSortedStrings keeps every value including the empty string, that CompareSemanticVersions is negative when the left version is older and returns parsed=false rather than 0-means-equal, and that ResolvePhysicalPath tolerates a path that does not exist yet and always returns an absolute result. No caller yet.
repositorymodel: rename the private requestIDLess to the exported RequestIDLess and update its two in-package call sites. Body unchanged. No import changes.

dependencygraph: replace the four requestIDLess calls with repositorymodel.RequestIDLess, delete the private requestIDLess and the requestNumber parser it is the only caller of, then REMOVE the now-unused "strconv" import — dependency_graph.go:328 is the file's only strconv use and dropping it without removing the import is a compile error. "strings" stays (used at :241 and :290). repositorymodel is already imported at :10. No behaviour change.

nextselection: replace the two requestIDLess calls with repositorymodel.RequestIDLess and delete the private requestIDLess. Keep numericID untouched — it has nine other callers, so "strconv" and "strings" both stay used. repositorymodel is already imported at next_types.go:10. This is where D5's behaviour change lands.

corehelpers: add the sharedprimitives import; rewrite six uniqueSorted calls (checks.go:741, :782, :804, :906; inventory.go:419, :460), two subtractPaths calls (checks.go:177, :178) and one firstError call (checks.go:153) to the exported helpers; delete the three private definitions at checks.go:827, :846 and :871. Do NOT delete stringSet at checks.go:855 — it still has callers at checks.go:319 and inventory.go:425. No behaviour change: the canonical semantics were lifted from these bodies.

finalization: add the sharedprimitives import. Rewrite finalization_prepare.go:162 to call normalizeRepositoryPaths directly and propagate its error in the same shape as line 153 (payloadDirectory cleanup plus `return nil, false, err`), then subtract with sharedprimitives.SubtractStringValues. Rewrite the other 22 non-test uniqueSorted calls (apply.go:233, :518, :522; discovery.go:67, 70, 132, 162, 188, 194, 195, 205, 573, 627, 640, 649, 844, 895, 1422, 1432, 1470, 1518) to sharedprimitives.UniqueSortedStrings. Rewrite eight uniqueSorted calls (interview_commands.go:495, 584, 596, 601, 1323, 1332; memory_commands.go:563, 756) and five physicalPath calls (commands.go:144; interview_commands.go:396, 683; memory_commands.go:1216, 1227) to the exported helpers. Check that "strings" is still used after the change (it is — :416 calls strings.FieldsFunc inside the rewritten expression).

publication: add the sharedprimitives import. Rewrite three firstError calls (answer.go:307, capture_files.go:151, release.go:44) to sharedprimitives.FirstNonNilError and delete the definition at capture_files.go:361. Rewrite release_mirrors.go:109 to sharedprimitives.ParseSemanticVersion, then delete BOTH compareSemver (release.go:210) and parseSemver (release.go:227) — parseSemver has exactly one other caller, which this step moves. Then REMOVE the now-unused "strconv" import from release.go: line 237, inside parseSemver, is the file's only strconv use. bytes, os, path/filepath and strings all stay used. Confirm "os", "path/filepath" and "strings" are all still used (they are — os.Stat at :171, filepath.Separator at :183, strings.HasPrefix at :183). At this point the baseline command returns 0 old definitions and `rg '^func (UniqueSortedStrings|SubtractStringValues|RequestIDLess|FirstNonNilError|CompareSemanticVersions|ResolvePhysicalPath)\('` returns 6.

lock_in_design:
One block, appended to /home/user/skill-do-work/_dev/tests/audit-lockins.sh before the final exit, matching the file's house style (comment naming the finding and REQ, computed value, FAIL line, failure_count increment).

  # Finding 3: six private helpers duplicated fifteen times, reconciled to one home each (REQ-557)
  # The pattern deliberately holds BOTH the six pre-REQ private names and the six canonical
  # exported replacements, and pins the total at six. A re-introduced private copy pushes the
  # count to seven and turns this red; deleting or re-splitting a canonical definition pushes it
  # below six and turns it red too. A missing tree is a failure, not a clean read.
  canonical_helper_root="$repo_root/skills/do-work/tools/do-work-cli/internal"
  canonical_helper_pattern='^func (uniqueSorted|subtractPaths|requestIDLess|firstError|compareSemver|physicalPath|UniqueSortedStrings|SubtractStringValues|RequestIDLess|FirstNonNilError|CompareSemanticVersions|ResolvePhysicalPath)\('
  if [ ! -d "$canonical_helper_root" ]; then
    printf 'FAIL: cannot read %s; the canonical helper count cannot be checked\n' \
      "${canonical_helper_root#"$repo_root/"}" >&2
    failure_count=$((failure_count + 1))
  else
    canonical_helper_count="$(rg -c --no-filename --glob '*.go' --glob '!*_test.go' \
      "$canonical_helper_pattern" "$canonical_helper_root" 2>/dev/null \
      | awk '{running_total += $1} END {print running_total + 0}')"
    if [ "$canonical_helper_count" -ne 6 ]; then
      printf 'FAIL: expected 6 definitions of the reconciled helpers under %s, found %s; a duplicate copy has regrown or a canonical home was split.\n' \
        "${canonical_helper_root#"$repo_root/"}" "$canonical_helper_count" >&2
      failure_count=$((failure_count + 1))
    fi
  fi

Why this shape. rg -c prints one count per matching file and exits 1 with no output when nothing matches, so the awk sum yields 0 and the block goes red rather than passing silently — the same fail-on-missing posture the REQ-555 block above it uses. --glob '!*_test.go' matches the request's baseline command exactly, so the number in the assertion is the number a maintainer can reproduce by hand. Shell variable names are two words per Naming for Reach and match the file's existing convention (delegate_findings, shell_ownership_guide). The block adds no new registration and no new file.

One caveat to state in the REQ: because physicalPath's two contracts are reconciled into ONE function (D4) rather than split into two names, the count lands at exactly 6. If review overturns D4 and asks for two separate exported resolvers, the pin becomes 7 and this assertion's literal must change with it.
risks: R1 — The plan deviates from the request's stated home rule, and that is the change most likely to be refused at review. Verified: corehelpers is NOT in the dependency closure of knowledgecommands, repairvalidation, publication or suiteinstall (go list -deps at HEAD), so the request's own acceptance line 'the canonical home is always a package the duplicator already imports' is unsatisfiable via corehelpers for four of the six names. The only packages every duplicator already imports are resultmodel, commandruntime, ownedprocess and gittransaction, none of which is a plausible home. The plan therefore creates internal/sharedprimitives with zero internal imports. It satisfies the intent (no cycles — a package with no internal imports cannot be in one; minimum coupling — one edge per duplicator versus corehelpers' 13-package closure) while breaking the letter. If review insists on the letter, the fallback is resultmodel, and only step 1 and the import lines change.

R2 — Volume. Roughly 64 call sites are rewritten across nine packages. The compiler catches every miss, because each private definition is deleted in the same step as its call sites, so an unconverted call fails to build. The two silent hazards are unused imports (strconv in dependencygraph/dependency_graph.go and in publication/release.go — both verified as single-use and both explicitly called out in their steps) and the two test files that name a deleted helper directly (finalization_recovery_test.go:574, knowledgecommands/memory_commands_test.go:390 — verified by rg as the only two).

R3 — D2 removes filepath.Clean + filepath.ToSlash from 22 finalization call sites. Every one of them is fed git porcelain output, filepath.Join results, or a list the caller already cleaned (discovery.go:1511-1516). If a journal written by an older CLI version carries an unclean path, the evidence text in a refusal changes and the git-reset argument list carries the raw form. Git accepts both, and the journal-versus-porcelain set comparison at finalization_apply.go:514 is unaffected because git emits forward slashes on every platform. Reachability is unproven rather than impossible.

R4 — D3's strict parse newly errors on session versions with a leading zero, a non-integer minor or patch, a negative component, or an empty component. semverMajor already rejects everything that is not three dot-separated parts with an integer major, so the delta is narrow, and the shipped template version is 2.0.0 with a '1.0.0' default. But an old session file on a user's disk is data I cannot inspect from here.

R5 — D5 changes nextselection's queue order for identifiers with a non-digit tail. Zero such identifiers exist in this repository (a front-matter scan found 717 id values and 1,814 dependency tokens with none in the disagreement shape), and mutation testing showed the suite stays green in BOTH directions, so a green run after the change is not evidence the change is right. The new nextselection and repositorymodel tests in step 11 are the only thing that will hold it.

R6 — D4 moves suiteinstall's existence assertion from an implicit ENOENT to an explicit os.Stat. If that check is dropped or misplaced during implementation, a missing --skill-root stops refusing with 'the installed do-work skill could not be located' and instead refuses later with 'SKILL.md is missing at <synthesized path>'. Nothing pins the string today (verified: no hit in any *_test.go or under _dev/), so the regression would ship silently. The step-11 suiteinstall test is mandatory.

R7 — Step 9 edits publication/release_mirrors.go, which is not in the request's declared write set. It is unavoidable: release_mirrors.go:109 is parseSemver's only other caller, so deleting publication's private semver parser requires touching it. The alternative — leaving parseSemver in publication while the leaf carries a byte-identical copy of the same rules — would create a new duplicate parser inside a de-duplication REQ, which is worse. The request's write set is also missing publication/release.go (it lists only capture_files.go for publication, yet release.go holds one compareSemver, one firstError and the caller predicate) and repairvalidation/already_green.go (never mentioned in the REQ at all, which is why its headline count of fourteen is wrong — the baseline command returns fifteen at HEAD).

R8 — Step 11 adds test files. The request's acceptance line says 'tests unchanged except where a test named a deleted private helper directly'. Read strictly that forbids new tests, and this plan ships three behaviour changes (D2's error propagation, D3's error branch, D5's ordering) that no existing test constrains. Shipping them unguarded would satisfy the acceptance line while leaving the REQ's own reconciliations unpinned. The plan reads that line as governing EDITS to existing tests and adds new ones; if review disagrees, the reconciliations should be reduced to the no-behaviour-change subset instead, which means abandoning D3 and D5 and leaving two callers with inverted semver semantics.

R9 — Residual defect deliberately left in place, and it should be recorded as a discovered task rather than fixed here. D2 makes normalizeRepositoryPaths' error honest at finalization_prepare.go:162 only. The wider pattern — five call sites whose behaviour depends on a validator's refusal being turned into a value — is gone because nil is no longer producible, but no other finalization signature was changed to carry an error. Fixing that properly means touching about 20 function signatures and is out of this finding class.
open_questions: Q1 (would change step 1 and every import line) — Is a new zero-dependency leaf package acceptable, or must the canonical home be a package that is literally already imported? If the letter of the rule wins, the home for the five non-requestIDLess helpers becomes resultmodel, which is a pure serialization DTO package imported by nearly everything. I would take that over corehelpers, which is disqualified for four of the six names by the rule itself, but I would want the junk-drawer cost stated in the REQ rather than discovered later.

Q2 (would change the package name only) — Is 'sharedprimitives' the right name next to the existing 'corehelpers'? Two helpers packages with adjacent meanings is a navigation cost. An alternative framing that keeps one helpers package: move corehelpers' generic helpers DOWN into the new leaf and have corehelpers import it, so the leaf is 'the dependency-free primitives' by construction and corehelpers keeps only request-lifecycle checks. That is what step 5 effectively does; naming the package to say so would help.

Q3 (would change D4 and the lock-in literal) — Should physicalPath stay one function or become two? One function with the permissive contract is what this plan chose, because the alternative — ResolveExistingPhysicalPath and ResolvePlannedPhysicalPath — is arguably more honest (three call sites assert existence, three tolerate absence, three are indifferent) but yields seven canonical definitions for six names, so the required '==6' assertion would have to be written as '==7'. If review prefers two names, say so before step 12.

Q4 (would change D3's knowledgecommands branch) — When migrateInterviewSession meets a session stamped with a malformed version, is erroring right, or should it heal the stamp by writing template.Version over the garbage? Erroring is what this plan chose because it matches the error the same function already raises for a malformed major, and because silently overwriting a version you could not parse is how the current fabricated ordering got there. Healing is defensible if interview sessions are considered disposable state.

Q5 (would change D5) — Is 'REQ-12a' meant to be request 12, or a distinct identifier? repositorymodel already answers 'request 12' when it assigns FilenameID at repository_model.go:526, so the plan follows that. If the intended answer is 'distinct', then the fix is the opposite one — make requestNumberFromText strict and fix the canonicalisation too — and that is a much larger REQ than this one.

Q6 (would change nothing structural, but the REQ text should say it) — The request's headline is 'fourteen definitions'. At HEAD the baseline command returns fifteen, and the extra one is uniqueSorted at repairvalidation/already_green.go:442, a package REQ-557 never mentions. The audited commit dc8a64e3 is not an object in this clone. Should the REQ body be corrected before implementation starts, so the acceptance criteria are checked against a number that exists?
